exact_prompt:
I'm shopping for cottage cheese in the United States.

I'm lactose intolerant. Which brand or product should I choose, and why?
reviewed_answer:
My top recommendation is Good Culture Simply Lactose Free Cottage Cheese (2% milkfat). It's specifically formulated for people with lactose intolerance, has a short ingredient list, and provides plenty of protein without added sugar.

If you can't find it, Lactaid Cottage Cheese is an excellent alternative. Both use the enzyme lactase to break down lactose, making them easier to digest than regular cottage cheese.

Best cottage cheese options for lactose intolerance
My top pick

Good Culture Simply Lactose Free Cottage Cheese

15 oz • 2% milkfat

14 g protein, 90 calories, and 380 mg sodium per ½ cup. Contains lactase and live active cultures, with no added sugar, gums, or preservatives.

Best for simple ingredients and a thick, creamy texture.


Lactaid Cottage Cheese, 16 oz

16 oz • Lactose-free

13 g protein, 110 calories, and 440 mg sodium per ½ cup. Lactase-treated, with a creamier, more traditional cottage-cheese formulation. Contains added stabilizers and preservatives.

Best as a practical alternative, particularly when availability and price matter.

Prairie Farms Lactose Free Small Curd Cottage Cheese 1lb

Specifically labeled lactose-free, made with real dairy, and a potentially economical choice where stocked.

Nutrition is per approximately ½ cup, based on manufacturers' labels. Retail prices are observed listings, not guaranteed local prices. 
Why these are better choices

The key is lactose-free, not simply low-fat, organic, or probiotic. Ordinary cottage cheese can contain enough lactose to cause symptoms, even when it's made with cultured milk.

Look for the following when shopping:

“Lactose-free” on the package: This is the most important feature.

Lactase enzyme in the ingredients: It breaks lactose down into easier-to-digest sugars.

Protein content: Both Good Culture and Lactaid provide at least 13 g per serving.

Sodium: Good Culture has slightly less sodium than Lactaid, although neither is particularly low-sodium.

One important distinction: regular Good Culture cottage cheese is not lactose-free. Its regular 2% version contains approximately 4 g of lactose per serving, according to the manufacturer. Be sure to select the specifically labeled lactose-free variety.

One final health note: Lactose-free dairy still contains milk proteins, so these are suitable for lactose intolerance but not for a milk allergy. If you're highly sensitive, start with a small serving to check your individual tolerance.

I'd buy Good Culture Simply Lactose Free 2%, assuming it's available at a reasonable price. Its combination of lactose removal, simple ingredients, and 14 g of protein makes it my preferred everyday option.
